title: Observability: cardinality guardrails for saturation metrics (label normalization + sampling)
author: Logan Wright
release_notes:
- Adds runtime guardrails to prevent high-cardinality saturation metrics from impacting Prometheus/OTel backends.
- Normalizes key labels (service/route/region/model) and drops/limits unsafe labels.
- Adds sampling for bursty per-host saturation series; emits visibility metrics for drops/samples.
description: Motivation: Collector scale tests for the incident-bot saturation snapshot surfaced a recurring issue: a handful of saturation metrics were being emitted with effectively unbounded label values (e.g., raw pod IDs / node names, per-request route variants, and occasionally experiment IDs leaking through). This creates an outsized cost in the telemetry pipeline and makes alerts/dashboards noisy and unreliable. This PR adds cardinality guardrails in the `redwood` metrics emission layer specifically for saturation signals (queue depth, throttling, scheduler contention, KV cache pressure), aligned with the saturation standard. Approach: (1) Label normalization: Introduce a small normalization layer for common dimensions: `service`, `region`, `cluster`, `route`, `model`, `gpu_pool`. This enforces a canonical format (lowercase, `-` separators), strips known-unsafe suffixes (pod hashes), and maps legacy synonyms (`us_east_1` -> `us-east-1`, `prod-use1` -> `use1-prod`). (2) Label allowlist + drop accounting: For the saturation metrics namespace, only a defined allowlist of labels is permitted. Any extra labels are dropped and counted via `metrics_guardrail_dropped_labels_total{metric=...,label=...}` plus a sampled log line (rate-limited) for debugging. (3) Series cap + sampling strategy: Add a soft cap on unique series per process for saturation metrics. Once the cap is exceeded, we keep emitting aggregated series at the safe dimensions and sample the remainder (default 1/N, N configurable) while emitting `metrics_guardrail_sampled_points_total{metric=...}`. This is intentionally fail-open: we still emit a usable signal rather than blocking request paths. (4) Tests + rollout safety: Adds unit tests for normalization edge cases and an integration-ish test that feeds synthetic high-cardinality label sets to verify we bound the number of emitted series. Default guardrails are enabled for saturation metrics only; other namespaces are unchanged. Notes: This is prompted by incident-bot collector load testing and by SUP-4933 investigations where noisy per-host metrics made queue-depth alerts less actionable. Follow-ups: Once this has baked, we can reuse the same guardrail helpers for change-annotation events and a few remaining runtime metrics with accidental pod/node labels.

conversation:
Allison Grant (review): The general direction looks good. Two asks: (1) please confirm the label allowlist matches the saturation standard (esp. `gpu_pool` vs `pool`) and (2) can we make the drop behavior visible without reading logs?
Logan Wright (author): Updated allowlist to include `gpu_pool` (and normalized legacy `pool` -> `gpu_pool`). Added `metrics_guardrail_dropped_labels_total` and `metrics_guardrail_sampled_points_total` with a small dashboard panel and an alert when drops spike.

Caleb Johnson (review): I’m concerned about sampling in exporters—could this make alerting flakey? Also, where is the cap enforced (per-process vs global)?
Logan Wright (author): Cap is per-process (exporter instance) to prevent local explosions; sampling only applies after cap is exceeded. Before cap, we emit all points. After cap, we still emit aggregated safe-dimension series at full fidelity (no sampling) and only sample the additional high-cardinality series that would otherwise blow up. Added a test to ensure aggregated series always survives.

Aisha Bello (review): Please ensure we don’t accidentally change existing label keys for dashboards in the short term. Do we need a transition period?
Logan Wright (author): Kept existing canonical keys for saturation dashboards; only normalizing values. Where we saw key mismatches (`pool`), we map to `gpu_pool` but keep emitting `gpu_pool` only for saturation metrics. Added a note in docs and a guardrail counter so SRE can see if something starts getting dropped.

Rafael Mendes (review): Can we tie this back to the incident-bot saturation collector so responders understand what happened if a section looks ‘thin’?
Logan Wright (author): Good call. Added a troubleshooting paragraph in `metrics_guardrails.md` that the bot/runbook can link to: if saturation context is missing per-host breakdowns, check guardrail counters + exporter logs, and rely on aggregated queue depth + throttling series.

Jacob Stein (review): Any risk this touches request path latency?
Logan Wright (author): Guardrail logic runs in the metrics emission path and is O(labels). Added a micro-benchmark in the PR notes: ~0.6–1.2us per emit under normal conditions. Also rate-limited logging to avoid hot loops.

Allison Grant (final): LGTM after latest changes. Thanks for adding the visibility counters + alert.
Caleb Johnson (final): Approving. Sampling behavior is reasonable with aggregated series preserved.
